messages:
ryan: 🚨 we're seeing a large traffic evacuation from us-east1 to us-west1 and several kv-cache shard metrics went silent in us-east1
maya: got it, which metrics are missing?
ryan: kvcache.hit_ratio and kvcache.latency per-shard are flatlined since 03:12 UTC for nodes in cluster-e-us1
cheng: checking prometheus — scrape targets for exporter-gpu-metrics-us1 are DOWN
elisabeth: terraform drift? any network ACL changes?
ryan: no config pushes in the window, looks like nodes were cordoned by autoscaler during an infra maintenance and exporter pod didn't reschedule
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1218. Priority: P2. Runbook: observability-loss -> follow restart-exporter
maya: restarting exporter daemonset on cluster-e-us1 now: `kubectl rollout restart ds/gpu-exporter -n infra-monitoring`
cheng: rolling, but kubelet is rejecting pull on one node due to registry auth error (401)
ryan: that explains the gap — partial rollout left some shards without exporters -> missing metrics and aggregated dashboards show gaps
elisabeth: can we attach a temporary scrape fallback? maybe scrape node-exporter for kvcache counters until gpu-exporter recovers
maya: adding node-exporter metrics to the prometheus scrape config for the affected job now, pushing a hotfix config via configmap
cheng: prom reload applied. Query to verify: `sum by (shard) (rate(kvcache_hits_total[5m]))` still shows zeros for shard-7 and shard-8
ryan: shard-7 was on node-17 which got cordoned then drained at 03:08; node-17 failed to rejoin due to kernel OOM killer earlier
elisabeth: OOM on node-17? oncall-ryan can you confirm node health and whether we should reprovision?
oncall-ryan: looking, node-17 is reporting kernel oom and docker crashloop; I'm provisioning replacement node (n-17-repl) and attaching it to the nodepool, ETA ~8m
maya: temporary grafana alert silence for missing kvcache series created so we don't get repeat noise :thumbsup:
cheng: exporters are now up on new nodes, prometheus shows targets healthy for exporter-gpu-metrics-us1
ryan: dashboards backfilled partially. but we lost fine-grained logs for the 03:08-03:20 window because kubelet logs were rotated and not sent to central logging due to a sidecar crash
elisabeth: that's the instrumentation gap — logs + metrics missing for the window. we need to ensure sidecar log-forwarder has restartPolicy and a crashloop guard
maya: opened PR: https://git.redwood/infra/observability/pulls/4821 -> changes: add livenessProbe + volume-backed buffer for log-forwarder, and fallback to aggregated-exporter endpoint when exporter missing
cheng: also adding a Prometheus recording rule to synthesize kvcache hit_ratio from node-exporter counters when exporter metrics absent (short-term mitigation)
oncall-ryan: new node is healthy, pods rescheduled, KV cache shard metrics restored and traffic rebalanced across regions
ryan: (typo) -- thanks all. postmortem action items noted:
- 1) add registry auth retries for daemonset pulls (maya)
- 2) durable buffer for log-forwarder sidecar (maya, PR#4821)
- 3) synthetic recording rules for exporter gaps (cheng)
- 4) autoscaler cordon-during-maintenance -> ensure staggered drain so exporters stay live (ryan)
- 5) add runbook step: fallback scrape node-exporter for kvcache counters (elisabeth)
elisabeth: I'll own the runbook update and add a checklist to verify backups of node logs before drain windows
maya: retro note: this caused ~12% increase in cross-region egress for 10m while traffic shifted — cost impact ~ $1200 estimate, putting cost tag on the incident
ops-bot: Incident updated: INC-2026-1218 -> status: mitigated. Follow-ups assigned.
ryan: thanks team. we'll schedule a short infra triage tomorrow to get fixes merged and tested in staging. good catch on fallback scrape and synthetic metrics. :wave:
